title: High-contrast scenes
summary: Deep shadows and bright highlights in one frame — something has to give.
why: The D7100's sensor holds about 13 stops; a sunlit scene with cave-dark shadows can span more. The meter averages the extremes and nails neither — highlights burn while shadows block up.

steps.text: Set the mode dial to A
Hold ±, spin the rear dial to −0.7
Shoot RAW so the shadows come back in post
For insurance, bracket 3 frames at 1 EV

pitfalls: Trust the blinkies, not the LCD preview — the screen lies in daylight.
levelUp: Expose for the highlights on purpose: spot-meter the brightest thing that matters, lock with AE-L, recompose. Shadows lift 2–3 stops in RAW; blown highlights are gone forever.
